messages:
elaine: quick heads-up — the ruby sampleapp README tells people to `gem install redwood-cli` but the installed bin is `redwood-cli` while our docs expect `redwood`. a user hit `No such file to load -- redwood-cli/main` when running `redwood` after install. anyone seen this?

sam: hm, can you paste the exact error + rubygems version?

elaine: paste: ```/usr/local/bin/redwood:23:in `require_relative': cannot load such file -- redwood-cli/main (LoadError)
from /usr/local/bin/redwood:23:in `<top (required)>'
ruby 3.1.2p20 (2024-01-01) + rubygems 3.3.6```

jonah: yup — rubygems 3.3 changed wrapper handling. we used to ship a `redwood` wrapper but the gemspec currently only exposes `redwood-cli`, so rubygems only generated that. packaging mismatch. quick workarounds: `gem install redwood-cli -n /usr/local/bin && ln -s /usr/local/bin/redwood-cli /usr/local/bin/redwood` or `bundle binstubs redwood-cli`.

maya: simple fix: update gemspec to include both executables and update the README to recommend `bundle exec redwood` or the canonical `redwood`. i can open a tiny PR to add `spec.executables = ["redwood-cli", "redwood"]` and a short note about rubygems versions. :+1:

sam: please tag me on the PR — i'll run macOS + musl CI quickly. saw similar installer flakes before.

devex-bot: CI job #34212 queued for branch/patch/readme-gem-exec

elaine: thanks — could we also add a one-liner fallback in quickstart: `ruby -S redwood` for system ruby weirdness?

jonah: SGTM. thanks for triaging!
